jobs.title: Director, Global Business Planning (FP&A)
jobs.description:
Your Opportunity at ARC’TERYX:

As the Director, Global Business Planning, you will serve as the connective tissue of Arc'teryx's global financial planning process. You will own the consolidation of all regional financial plans, including annual budgets and quarterly forecasts, into a coherent, enterprise-wide view, enabling leadership to make informed decisions with speed and confidence. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role that operates at the intersection of financial planning, strategic insight, and executive communication.

You will serve as the primary architect of our financial planning calendar and cadence, partnering closely with regional and global FP&A teams to drive alignment, consistency, and analytical rigor across the enterprise. You will also own the financial systems infrastructure, reporting frameworks, and capital planning processes that power Arc'teryx's ability to plan and perform at a global scale.

This role is based out of our North Vancouver office. Candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

Meet Your Future Team:

The Global FP&A team at Arc'teryx sits at the center of enterprise financial decision-making. We are responsible for translating regional and functional performance into a unified financial narrative, providing leadership with the clarity to review past results, understand business drivers, and plan confidently for the future. We work closely with regional finance partners across North America, China, EMEA, and APAC, as well as functional leaders across the business, to deliver insights that matter.

If you were in the Director, Global Business Planning role now, here are some of the core activities you would be doing:

Owning the end-to-end consolidation of all regional financial plans, including annual budgets and quarterly forecasts, into an integrated global view across P&L, and capital expenditures

Leading enterprise-wide variance analysis, comparing actuals to budget and forecast, and synthesizing insights into clear, executive-ready commentary that explains the 'so what' behind the numbers

Serving as the primary finance lead for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBR), Board of Directors (BOD) materials, and investor-facing financial narratives, partnering closely with the CFO and VP of FP&A on preparation and delivery

Building and maintaining the global financial planning calendar, coordinating planning cycles across regional FP&A teams to ensure timely, consistent, and high-quality submissions

Owning and continuously improving Arc'teryx's financial systems infrastructure, including OneStream, PowerBI, and Oracle, to ensure accurate, efficient, and scalable financial reporting and planning capabilities

Developing and managing enterprise-level financial analytics and insights capabilities, including standardized KPI frameworks, executive dashboards, and performance reporting tools

Leading capital planning processes, including tracking of capital expenditure budgets, return-on-investment analysis, and reporting to senior leadership and the Board

Acting as a key connector between regional FP&A teams and global finance leadership, fostering collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and best practice alignment across geographies

Driving continuous improvement in planning processes, reporting accuracy, and analytical capabilities through automation, systems enhancements, and process redesign

Supporting ad-hoc strategic analysis requests from executive leadership, including scenario modelling, business case development, and financial due diligence

Here are some of the things you could be working on in the future:

Building Arc'teryx's next-generation financial planning and reporting infrastructure to support the company's growth and increased organizational complexity

Expanding the Global FP&A team's analytics capabilities through AI-driven forecasting, predictive modelling, and automated insight generation

Acting as a thought partner to the CFO and C-suite on capital allocation priorities, financial strategy, and enterprise planning governance

Representing Global FP&A in cross-functional initiatives related to ERP transformation, data strategy, and digital finance evolution

Are you our next Director, Global Business Planning?

You have 10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance, with at least 3 years in a senior leadership role with global or multi-regional scope

You have a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, or equivalent, and ideally hold a CPA, CFA, or MBA

You have deep expertise in financial consolidation and enterprise planning processes, budget cycles, quarterly forecasts, and long-range plans, across multiple business units or geographies

You have a strong command of financial systems and planning tools (OneStream, Oracle, SAP, or equivalent), with demonstrated ability to drive systems improvements and reporting automation

You are an exceptional communicator who can translate complex financial data into clear, compelling narratives for executive and Board-level audiences

You have experience preparing and supporting QBR and Board of Directors materials, with an understanding of what leadership needs to make high-stakes decisions

You have advanced analytical and modelling skills, with proficiency in Excel, PowerBI, and other data visualization tools

You are a collaborative, trust-building leader who can influence without authority and drive alignment across regional and functional teams

You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and can manage multiple high-priority workstreams simultaneously without sacrificing quality

You are proactive in identifying the root cause of issues and developing scalable, cross-functional solutions

You inspire breakthrough thinking and continuous improvement in the teams and processes you touch

Your passion for your work is paralleled by your passion for getting outside and living it

Compensation:
The salary range for this role is CAD$149,000 - CAD$195,000 

Total Rewards

Most new team members join between the start and midpoint of the range, where you can contribute right away while continuing to grow your craft, your collaborations, and your impact at Arc’teryx. This range reflects market alignment and the scope of the role. Individual pay is determined by your skills, experience, and level of responsibility.

We’re committed to fair, equitable, and competitive pay, reviewed regularly to ensure internal alignment and market relevance. Transparency is part of how we follow through on our commitments and how we honour the value you bring to our team.

In addition to base pay, Arc’teryx supports people through benefits designed to sustain both work and life:

Health & wellbeing
- Extended health, dental, and vision coverage, including mental health support, fertility benefits, gender-affirming care and a 24/7 Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Financial wellbeing
- RRSP matching and eligibility for Arc'teryx Annual Incentive Plan and access to Employee Stock Purchase program (ESPP) where applicable.

Time & Flexibilit
y - Paid time off, wellness time, and No Wasted Day program (dedicated paid days to get outside & explore).

Family support
- Parental leave top-up and a nesting period for new parents.

Growth, community & gear
- Professional development opportunities, Arc'teryx Academies (outdoor skill-building events) , Employee Belonging Councils, and access to employee discounts and Pro Deals (exclusive discounted pricing on gear).
  *Eligibility for certain programs may vary by role.

Equal Opportunity

Arc’teryx is committed to actively creating and fostering a culture of inclusivity where voices are heard, people are seen, and values are respected. We care about the uniqueness of our applicants, employees, and guests, and we do so in a safe space fueled by curiosity and acceptance. 

Creating an inclusive workplace is connected to our core value Do Right while also having the added benefit of helping make our business better. We believe inclusion helps us to create a healthier, happier workplace, drive creativity and innovation, and reflect the communities where we operate.  

All applicants, employees, and guests can expect equality of opportunity and fair treatment in alignment with our values.

Leave it Better

We believe that the mountains transform us, that how we adventure matters, and that there’s always a better way. 

Join us in creating positive change in ourselves, our communities, and the world. 

Live it. Get out there - the mountains make us better 
Disruptive evolution . In pursuit of better. Always. 
Commit.  We set bold objectives and see them through.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
WESTERN CANADA (NORTH)

Salary up to $125,000

(Hybrid/housing & relocation assistance available)

About The Role

Our client, a First Nation located in the North within Western Canada is currently seeking a Director of Finance to join their team. Reporting directly to the CAO and working on behalf of the Nation and its community members, the Director of Finance is responsible for the day-to-day accounting and financial management, oversight of the financial administration and ensuring compliance with accounting standards. The Director of Finance plays a critical role in supporting continued growth, providing financial insight and strategic advice in partnership with the CAO, and is hands on in their direct responsibilities of financial reporting, budgeting and internal controls.

Key Responsibilities

Budgeting & Financial Planning

Lead the development and integration of the annual budget
Consolidate department budgets, evaluate accuracy and alignment with strategic goals.
Create multi-year financial plan, capital plans, and risk management plans for presentation and CAO review

Financial Reporting

Prepare and present monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, and ad hoc financial reports
Develop financial highlights memos and analysis on financial performance and emerging risks.
Preparation of audit schedules and ensure compliance with accounting standards.
Process funding requirements and ensure funding reporting is submitted on time
Oversee payroll and benefits financial transactions and reporting in accordance with legislation

Cash & Bank Management

Oversee bank accounts, including approvals for opening/closing accounts, and ensure monthly reconciliation.
Ensure proper segregation of duties in all cash-handling and banking activities.
Supervise the preparation of cheque runs and ensure authorization procedures are followed.
Oversee Nation’s pension plan and communicate directly with brokers and educate members

Audit & Risk Management

Coordinate preparation for annual audits and support the external auditor with required documentation.
Lead financial risk assessments and reporting, ensuring mitigation strategies are in place.
Ensure that financial irregularities, breaches, and concerns are reported, investigated, and addressed appropriately.

Leadership & Staff Supervision

Collaborate with Department Managers to ensure timely and accurate budget submissions and financial updates.

Lead and mentor accounting and finance staff and provide training and guidance

Skills And Qualifications

Education & Experience

A degree in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline; CPA designation is preferred
5+ years of financial management experience, ideally in a First Nation, non-profit, or public sector environment.
Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, budgeting, strategic planning, and compliance.

Skills & Knowledge

In-depth understanding of accounting principles, internal control systems, and financial reporting.
Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Proficiency in financial management systems (e.g., Sage Intact) and Microsoft Office Suite.
Knowledge of Indigenous governance, funding mechanisms, and financial frameworks is an asset.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Hybrid combination of remote and on-site position with occasional overtime during peak reporting periods.
Interaction with Nation Members, staff, auditors, funders, and external stakeholders.
Must maintain confidentiality, professionalism, and cultural sensitivity always.

You may also apply directly by sending your resume to Sabine Bell at sabine.bell@mnp.ca and reference First Nation Director of Finance in the subject line.
